action_summary: Reduce primary spring infections; leaf-litter breakdown; timed protectant/SI fungicides.
source_name: UC IPM Pest Management Guidelines — Apple
evidence_summary: 'The main objective in scab management is the reduction or prevention of primary infections in spring.'

action_summary: Sterol-inhibitor fungicides; resistant apple/juniper cultivars; gall removal (limited).
evidence_summary: 'Fungicide application to manage cedar-apple rust is commonly included in the disease management programs of many apple production systems.'
review_notes: No UC IPM page (eastern-US disease); EPPO GYMNJV is taxonomy-only.

action_summary: Partial-resistance hybrids; rotation + residue management; fungicide VT–R2 on susceptible hybrids.
evidence_summary: 'Hybrids with partial resistance to GLS are available. Ask your seed supplier for these hybrids.'
review_notes: Not covered by UC IPM corn; independently spot-verified.

action_summary: Resistant hybrids (most effective); rotation 1–2 yr; tillage; fungicide at tasseling/silking.
evidence_summary: 'Planting resistant hybrids is the most effective method for controlling NCLB.'
review_notes: UC IPM corn lists only a different Exserohilum root rot (not cited).

action_summary: Resistant hybrids; fungicides generally not required under California conditions.
source_name: UC IPM Pest Management Guidelines — Corn (Common Rust)
evidence_summary: 'Use resistant hybrids to prevent common rust.'

action_summary: Optimum growing conditions; later-maturing varieties; monitor; fungicide 7–10 d when justified.
source_name: UC IPM Pest Management Guidelines — Potato (Early Blight)
evidence_summary: 'Early blight can be minimized by maintaining optimum growing conditions, including proper fertilization, irrigation, and management of other pests.'

action_summary: Eliminate cull piles/volunteers; certified seed; preventive fungicide 7–10 d; vine kill before harvest.
source_name: UC IPM Pest Management Guidelines — Potato (Late Blight)
evidence_summary: 'Late blight is controlled by eliminating cull piles and volunteer potatoes, using proper harvesting and storage practices, and applying fungicides when necessary.'
review_notes: OOMYCETE (water mould), not a true fungus; UC IPM prose loosely says 'fungus'. Maps to fungicide per brief §3.1.

action_summary: Resistant varieties; sanitation; weed control; treat at first symptoms, alternate fungicide MOA.
source_name: UC IPM Pest Management Guidelines — Cucurbits (Powdery Mildew)
evidence_summary: 'Plant resistant varieties, follow good sanitation practices, and control weeds.'

action_summary: Sanitation — remove mummies + prune diseased wood; fungicides early bloom to 3–4 wk after bloom.
evidence_summary: 'Fungicides should be sprayed during the period from early bloom through three to four weeks after bloom.'
review_notes: No UC IPM page (minor CA disease); EPPO GUIGBI is taxonomy-only.

action_summary: Destroy volunteer/nightshade hosts; rotation; protectant fungicides (chlorothalonil, mancozeb, copper).
source_name: UC IPM Pest Management Guidelines — Tomato (Early Blight)
evidence_summary: 'Destroy nightshades and volunteer tomato and potato plants. Proper crop rotation is important...'

action_summary: Sanitation; rotate away from tomato 2+ yr; reduce leaf wetness; preventive fungicides.
evidence_summary: 'Septoria leaf spot is caused by the fungus Septoria lycopersici.' / 'Rotate away from tomato for 2 or more years.'
review_notes: No UC IPM page for tomato Septoria; .edu extension fallback.

action_summary: Pathogen-free seed/transplants (best); avoid sprinklers; rotate nonhost; copper protectant only.
source_name: UC IPM Pest Management Guidelines — Tomato (Bacterial Spot)
evidence_summary: 'Using pathogen-free seed and disease-free transplants, when possible, is the best way to avoid bacterial spot on tomato.'
review_notes: Modern taxonomy splits bacterial-spot xanthomonads into ~4 species.

action_summary: Resistant varieties; remove volunteers; avoid sprinklers; protectant fungicide before onset.
source_name: UC IPM Pest Management Guidelines — Tomato (Late Blight)
evidence_summary: 'Apply a protectant fungicide before disease development begins...'
review_notes: OOMYCETE, not a true fungus. Maps to fungicide per brief §3.1.

pathogen_name: Tomato yellow leaf curl virus (TYLCV, begomovirus)
action_summary: Resistant varieties; virus-/whitefly-free transplants; whitefly control; rogue infected plants.
source_name: UC IPM Pest Management Guidelines — Tomato (Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl)
evidence_summary: 'Select TYLCV-resistant varieties. Use virus- and whitefly-free transplants.'
review_notes: Whitefly (Bemisia)-transmitted -> cleanly maps to remove_vector. Independently spot-verified.

action_summary: Resistant (Cf-gene) varieties; lower humidity (spacing/airflow); sanitation; preventive fungicides.
evidence_summary: 'Leaf mold is caused by the fungus Fulvia fulva' / 'Fungicides are preventatives, not curatives.'
review_notes: No UC IPM leaf-mold page; university IPM fallback.

action_summary: Indexed/treated seed or clean transplants; rotate out of peppers ≥1 yr; drip not overhead; copper.
source_name: UC IPM Pest Management Guidelines — Peppers (Bacterial Spot)
evidence_summary: 'Use indexed pathogen-negative seed, treated seed, or disease-free transplants. Rotate out of peppers for at least 1 year.'

action_summary: Treated seed; extreme sanitation; resistant cultivars. Mechanically transmitted — NOT insect-vectored.
source_name: UC IPM Pest Management Guidelines — Tomato (Tobacco Mosaic)
evidence_summary: 'Use seed that has been treated to eliminate seedborne inoculum. Extreme sanitation is needed.'
review_notes: AMBIGUOUS: viral, but no insect vector to remove — the 'control vector' half of remove_vector does not apply; management is seed treatment + roguing/sanitation. Reviewer must decide remove_vector vs a sanitation action.

dataset_class: Tomato two spotted spider mites leaf
action_summary: Conserve natural enemies; water sprays; selective miticides (soap/oil) only when needed; monitor.
source_name: UC IPM Pest Notes — Spider Mites
evidence_summary: 'If a treatment for mites is necessary, use selective materials, preferably insecticidal soap or insecticidal oil.'
review_notes: Excluded under policy:arthropod-pest-scope-v1 (reports/ARTHROPOD_PEST_EVALUATION_SCOPE.md): Tetranychus urticae is an arthropod pest, not a plant pathogen. The class remains diagnosis-eligible and its images and manifest rows are retained; it is out of scope for disease-action and risk-weighted disease evaluation, so no canonical action-mapping row is emitted. Reviewed by human_reviewer_1.
